headline: Coatue says spending on AI could reach $2.8 trillion by 2028 and will need its own version of the US mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 2: a forecast from an investment firm, carried by one secondary outlet whose text could not be read, with no figures behind it.
importance_line: What changed is a forecast that AI spending could reach $2.8 trillion by 2028 and need its own Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which would matter first to savers and pension holders whose money is tied to AI-linked shares and bonds, then to lenders and AI builders, and the doubt is that it is one firm's projection reported second-hand, and its assumptions are not known.
summary: Dealroom, a startup and venture-capital data platform, reports that Coatue, a US investment firm, says capital spending on AI could reach $2.8 trillion by 2028 and will need its own equivalent of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the government-backed US mortgage-finance companies.
notes: Headline only: Dealroom page blocked (HTTP 403) and no other outlet found. Dealroom is the only outlet; Coatue is the originator of the forecast. What Coatue means by the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac comparison is not known.
